clue.text: Dashed off and printed a newspaper leader

parts.note: to print something with a mark or die is to stamp it
the leader of a newspaper is its editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: Someone rushed out and ran off the front-page editorial of a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed off' looks like hurried writing, but it is the definition: ran off in a panic like a herd. 'Leader' suggests an editorial; here it is the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To stampede is to rush away in a sudden panicked flight, as cattle do.

clue.text: It's too much for the players

definitions.text: It's too much for the players

parts.words: It's too much for the players
parts.note: an Italian direction printed on sheet music telling musicians not to overdo a tempo or effect

explanation.surface: Something is more than the performers can cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests actors or sportsmen; here they are musicians, reading a score marked in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Troppo is the Italian musical term meaning excessively, used in directions such as allegro ma non troppo.

clue.text: An actor needing no prompting

parts.note: a performer in a traditional silent play has no lines to forget, since keeping mum is the whole act

explanation.surface: A performer so well rehearsed that the prompter can relax.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a word-perfect actor; really it is one who never speaks, so has no lines to be prompted with. MUM is British for silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mummer is an actor in a traditional mime or folk play, performed without words.

clue.text: Recruit's silent break

indicators.note: the letters of the word silent are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A new soldier's quiet interlude away from the drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a noun, a rest period; it is the anagram signal on SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone is to sign them up, as in joining the armed forces.

clue.text: The characteristic nature of a German city engineer

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Describing what typifies an engineer from a German town.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the intrinsic quality that makes a thing what it is.

clue.text: Show-ring pronouncement

parts.note: to show something is to manifest it
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: An announcement made at a show-ring, as at a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show-ring' reads as one thing, an arena for animals; split it into a verb and a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public declaration of policy or aims.

clue.text: A real let-down!

parts.note: taken literally, letting air out of a tyre or balloon until it goes down

explanation.surface: Something proved very disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as disappointment; literally it is the letting out of air. The word also means an economic fall in prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Deflation is the release of air from something inflated, and figuratively a sudden loss of confidence.

clue.text: Getting coppers to secure twisters and bring charges

parts.note: coppers are small change, pennies, abbreviated P

indicators.note: the words to secure are twisted, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Police getting hold of tornado-chasing crooks and charging them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' wants to be police; it is pennies. 'Twisters' reads as crooks but signals that TO SECURE is jumbled to ROSECUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute is to institute legal proceedings against someone for an offence.

clue.text: How to progress rapidly in one's line of work

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hurtle along; as a noun it names an occupation pursued through life.

clue.text: Give official recognition to models of realism

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters of the words are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: Endorsing exemplary works of realist art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' looks like a noun, examples; it is a verb telling you to reshape OF REALISM.
explanation.definitionFit: To formalise something is to make it official or give it a fixed structure.

clue.text: Submits returns

definitions.meaning: profits or produce, as from an investment

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means gives in; the plural noun means the income an investment produces.

clue.text: Satisfying vegetables served in a sound container

indicators.note: the vegetables are dished up inside another word, as food goes in a dish

parts.note: a ping is a short ringing sound
peas are vegetables

explanation.surface: Tasty vegetables brought out in a sturdy bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective, sturdy; it is a noun, PING. PEAS go inside PING after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeasing means placating or pacifying someone by meeting their demands.

clue.text: The language of this French officer in charge!

parts.note: ce is French for this
Lt is short for lieutenant

explanation.surface: Asking what tongue a French officer in command speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures one French officer; split it into French 'this', a lieutenant, and the letters for in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is a language family including Irish, Welsh and Breton, the last spoken in France.

clue.text: They have no sense of duty

definitions.text: They have no sense of duty

parts.words: They have no sense of duty
parts.note: duty here is the customs tax on imported goods, which these people avoid paying

explanation.surface: Describing irresponsible people who shirk their obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' reads as moral obligation; it is the tax levied at customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugglers bring goods across borders secretly to evade the customs charges owed on them.

clue.text: Involving possibly ten in a bad way

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of ten may be arranged another way

parts.note: ailing means unwell, in poor condition

explanation.surface: Ten people are in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns TEN into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Entailing means necessarily bringing about or requiring as a consequence.

clue.text: With private transport, people will be in the pink!

parts.note: a car is a private vehicle
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Owning a car will make everyone healthy and happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' reads as the idiom for healthy; the pink is a garden flower, of which this is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are flowers of the genus Dianthus, and the carnation is the best known of them.

clue.text: The Roman cross

parts.note: the cross-shaped letter X is the Roman numeral for this number

explanation.surface: Referring to a cross as used in Rome, perhaps a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a religious symbol; the cross is X, which Romans used as a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman numerals X, a cross-shaped letter, stands for this number.

clue.text: Initially the English aristocracy's drink

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: The beverage first favoured by the English upper class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like 'at first' in the history; it picks the first letters of THE, ENGLISH and ARISTOCRACY'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot drink brewed from leaves, famously British.

clue.text: A refusal to be overweight

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone declines to put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overweight' looks like one word; split it so 'over' turns TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is a negative response; this word is the negative particle used in declining.

clue.text: Sanction individual appointment

parts.note: a man is an individual person
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Approving a single person's appointment to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appointment' suggests a job; it is a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official authorisation or command to act.

clue.text: Letters sent to a frontier station?

parts.note: letters that have been sent are out, dispatched
letters collectively are post, the mail

explanation.surface: Mail dispatched to a remote border garrison.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures mail to soldiers; read it as post that has gone out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small military camp or settlement at a distant border.

clue.text: A court's decree

explanation.surface: A judgment issued by a court.
explanation.definitionFit: An act is a law passed by a legislature, a formal decree.

clue.text: Anxiety about one-time British service

parts.note: C, from Latin circa, means about
one-time means former, formerly, once
the RN, the Royal Navy, is a British armed service

explanation.surface: Worry over a British service that no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time British service' reads as one defunct institution; split it into ONCE and RN, the Royal Navy, the senior British armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: Concern is worry or unease about something.

clue.text: Old lady getting tied in a knot

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a grandmother
describing a type of reef knot tied the wrong way, a slipping knot named after a grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly woman getting into a tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a familiar word for grandmother, and also names a badly tied reef knot.

clue.text: A painter taking some care — no irresponsible worker

indicators.note: the painter takes only a part of the words that follow, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A careful artist, never a reckless workman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts a careful painter with a careless workman; the letters run across CARE NO IRresponsible.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Remove the cad for agitating

indicators.note: agitating means shaking up, so the letters of the cad are stirred into new order

explanation.surface: Get rid of the bounder for stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitating' reads as the cad's offence; it signals that THE CAD is shaken up. A cad is an old British term for a dishonourable man.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach is to unfasten or separate something from what holds it.

clue.text: Asserts upturn's done away with a worry

indicators.note: done away with means the letter given by a is removed
in a down clue an upturn reads the word asserts from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Someone claims a recovery has eliminated a concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upturn's' turns ASSERTS into STRESSA; 'done away with' then removes the A. 'Upturn' looks like an economic recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental strain or anxiety.

clue.text: Bury sets out to offer attractions

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: out means the letters of sets are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: The town of Bury lays out its tourist sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town; it is a verb. 'Out' rearranges SETS into ESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Interests are things that engage attention or curiosity.

clue.text: The little minx, left with nothing, turned tail

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: turned means the letters of tail are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: A naughty girl, abandoned with nothing, ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned tail' looks like fleeing; 'turned' rearranges TAIL into ITA. The definition refers to the title character of Nabokov's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita, from Nabokov's novel, is a byword for a precociously seductive young girl.

clue.text: Honoured for architectural style

definitions.meaning: the ... style is the middle phase of English Gothic architecture

explanation.walkthrough: Decorated is the name for English Gothic building of roughly 1290 to 1350, with ornate window tracery.
explanation.definitionFit: It means awarded a medal, and names a period of English Gothic church building.

clue.text: The money demanded drove doctors back

parts.note: drove means ran, as in operated or drove a business

indicators.note: back means the word for doctors is read backwards

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, doctors

explanation.surface: A kidnapper's demand pushed medics into retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' looks like steering a car; it is RAN. 'Back' turns MOS into SOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is the sum demanded for the release of a captive.

clue.text: No government would please him!

parts.note: read not as a fussy voter but as someone who wants there to be no government at all

explanation.surface: A man impossible to satisfy with any administration.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a perpetual grumbler; literally, the absence of government is what he wants.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist believes in abolishing the state and all rule.
